articles.title: UTILITY OF INDOCYANINE GREEN FLUORESCENCE IMAGING IN BURN MANAGEMENT: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: The implementation of near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging using indocyanine green (ICG) has seen a rising implementation in burn care in recent years, with expanding clinical indications and increasing evidence supporting its use. A systematic review was carried out following PRISMA guidelines, employing PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, and EMBASE databases to locate studies on the perioperative use of ICG in burn patients. Two independent reviewers assessed all articles for eligibility based on predefined inclusion criteria. Extracted data included study characteristics, patient demographics, clinical indications, ICG dosing regimens, administration timing, and reported perioperative outcomes. A total of 12 studies enrolling 204 burn patients, published between 1995 and 2025, were included for qualitative synthesis. Of these, 7 (58.3%) were prospective, single-center experimental studies; 3 (25%) were prospective, multicenter, blinded trials; 1 (8.3%) was a retrospective study; and 1 (8.3%) was a case series. The primary clinical uses of ICG in burn management included: assessment of burn depth reported in 6 studies, intraoperative delineation of necrotic tissue requiring excision in 3 studies, utility of ICG in liver function measurement in 2 studies and another research analyzed the estimation of plasma volume in burn patients. ICG fluorescence imaging is a promising adjunctive tool for burn assessment, particularly in identifying non-perfused tissue. It enhances the ability to accurately assess burn depth and helps to determine surgical margins during burn excision. Furthermore, ICG pharmacokinetics may provide insight into liver involvement and prognostic outlook in severe burn cases. However, its current role remains complementary to clinical evaluation. Further standardized and high-quality studies are required to define its diagnostic accuracy and clinical impact.

articles.title: Bridging the Evidence Gap: A Call to Action for Anticoagulation Research in Pediatric Burned Patients on Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Although early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improves respiratory complications in unburned populations, it remains a rarely utilized rescue therapy in pediatric burn care, averaging just 3 to 6 cases annually worldwide despite a promising 53-62% survival rate. This underutilization stems from a profound therapeutic paradox: the high bleeding risks and need for coagulation inherent to burn wounds with necessary surgical debridement directly conflict with the systemic anticoagulation required to prevent ECMO circuit thrombosis. Importantly, emerging evidence demonstrates that systemic anticoagulation may not be an absolute requirement for veno-venous ECMO. Despite this, no guidance exists for anticoagulation management specifically in pediatric burned patients. A scoping review spanning three databases identified no studies describing a coagulation strategy developed or validated for this population. Addressing this evidence gap is essential to safely transition ECMO from a late rescue modality to an earlier, evidence-based intervention capable of reducing mortality in this patient population. We therefore call for (1) a multicenter collaboration to aggregate sufficient case volume for meaningful analysis; (2) a prospective collection of serial viscoelastic and conventional coagulation data in pediatric burned patients on ECMO to characterize the temporal evolution of coagulopathy on circuit; and (3) the development and validation of coagulation management protocols tailored to this population. Until such evidence exists, pediatric burned patients will continue to be denied a therapy that offers meaningful survival-not because ECMO does not work-but because we have not yet determined how best to manage coagulation while on circuit.

articles.title: Understanding Functional Recovery in Burn Survivors Aged 80 Years and Older: A Burn Model System Study.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: The global demographic shift toward an aging population is transforming burn care, yet the "oldest old" (adults ≥80 years) remain poorly understood. Standard geriatric guidelines are not specific to this subgroup, a group exhibiting unique physiological needs and vulnerabilities. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the Burn Model System (BMS) National Database for adults aged 80 years or older (N=104).1 Physical Function, Ability to Participate in Social Roles, and Pain Interference were assessed at 6 and 12 months post-burn and compared to pre-burn and US population norm (aged ≥75 years) data. Despite sustaining moderate injuries (Mean TBSA: 11.7%), our cohort required prolonged hospitalization (Mean: 26.9 days). We identified a functional recovery paradox: while Physical Function scores were low (40.1) at 12 months, Social Roles scores were average (50.0 at 6 months and 51.9 at 12 months). Notably, referral to inpatient rehabilitation (IPR) was highly variable (8.6% to 42.1%) and correlated strongly with social support; patients living alone were three times less likely to receive IPR than those with co-habitants (17.7% vs 61.7%). In conclusion, burn survivors aged 80 years and older face persistent reduction in physical function but demonstrate resilience in maintaining social roles, suggesting that slow physical recovery does not preclude quality of life. Prolonged acute hospitalizations and variable IPR access highlight the need for geriatric-specific guidelines to address the unique physiological, social, and systemic barriers that challenge the "oldest old."

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of combined MPFL-reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using hamstring autograft versus isolated MPFL in adolescents with patella alta: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Patella alta is a major risk factor for recurrent patellar dislocation in adolescents. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of isolated medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction with those of MPFL reconstruction augmented by medial patellotibial ligament (MPTL)-distalization, both using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft, in adolescent patients with patella alta. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 28 adolescent patients (mean age 11.2 ± 1.6 years; 9 males, 19 females) treated for recurrent patellar dislocation between May 2020 and July 2025. All patients had patella alta (Caton-Deschamps index > 1.2) and a history of at least one dislocation, with varying degrees of trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types A-B). All patients underwent MPFL reconstruction using a semitendinosus hamstring autograft harvested with preservation of its native distal tibial insertion, fixed via a single oblique transpatellar tunnel and femoral interference-screw fixation proximal to the distal femoral physis. Group A (n=14) underwent isolated MPFL reconstruction. Group B (n=14) underwent the same MPFL reconstruction with an additional MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization step using the same graft, secured by trans-osseous periosteal suture at the lateral patella. Surgical techniques emphasized physeal spare during reconstruction. Preoperative and postoperative assessments included the Kujala score, Lysholm score, Caton-Deschamps index, and sulcus angle. Follow-up averaged 12- 24 months. CT was performed using a low-dose pediatric protocol specifically for TT-TG measurement and trochlear bony morphology; MRI was used for soft-tissue and cartilage assessment. Group assignment was not randomized; patients with more pronounced patella alta and higher-grade clinical instability were preferentially treated with the combined procedure. Both groups showed significant improvements in functional scores. In Group (A), Kujala scores improved from 59.3 ± 8.3 to 84.3 ± 5.1, and Lysholm scores from 50.3 ± 7.5 to 74.7 ± 9.3. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.27 to 1.20. In Group (B), Kujala scores improved from 56.2 ± 7.4 to 88.9 ± 4.5, and Lysholm scores from 51.4 ± 7.6 to 87.4 ± 6.2. Caton-Deschamps index decreased from 1.28 to 1.11, indicating better patellar height correction. Complications occurred in 36% of Group A and 21% of Group B. Recurrent instability occurred in 2 patients (14%) in Group A and 1 patient (7%) in Group B; all were subluxation episodes managed non-operatively, and no revision surgery was required. This study demonstrated that MPFL reconstruction with MPTL-augmenting patellar distalization using a hamstring autograft yields greater functional improvements, superior patella alta correction, and fewer complications compared to isolated MPFL reconstruction in adolescents with recurrent patellar instability. Retrospective comparative study; level IV. Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study is a retrospective comparative cohort study and does not meet the definition of a clinical trial as per the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) guidelines, as it involves retrospective analysis of routinely collected clinical data without prospective intervention or randomization.

articles.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs. Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate. DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A). Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

articles.title: Quantitative decision-support strategies to enhance emergency medical service accessibility in high-risk freeway tunnels.
articles.abstract: Crashes inside road tunnels often result in more severe outcomes due to spatial constraints that delay prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) access. Emergency evacuation facilities, such as cross passages and emergency parking areas, are critical for ensuring timely EMS response during traffic congestion caused by in-tunnel crashes. This study presents a quantitative approach to develop targeted strategies for enhancing such facilities to improve EMS accessibility in tunnels. Nationwide in-tunnel crash data from Korean freeways over a four-year period were analyzed, and the limited number of severe crash cases was addressed using SMOTE-based data augmentation to balance severity levels in the prediction model. A SHAP-based XGBoost classifier was applied to identify the influence of key features related to EMS accessibility and emergency evacuation facilities on crash severity. The results showed that crashes occurring more than 1 km from the tunnel entrance and EMS response coverage within a 10-15 km range have a significant impact on increasing crash severity. The presence of emergency cross passages, three or more lanes, emergency parking areas, and properly spaced CCTV installations were found to help reduce crash severity. Based on these findings, tunnels with particularly limited EMS accessibility were prioritized, and tailored facility improvement measures were proposed. This study provides quantitative evidence to guide cost-effective upgrades of tunnel emergency evacuation facilities, enhancing prehospital EMS accessibility and emergency preparedness. The proposed methodology can also support decision-making on implementing road tunnel safety improvement policies.

articles.title: Community Paramedics Addressing the Evolving Opioid Crisis: A Case Series Addressing the Kratom Derivatives 7-Hydroxymitragynine and MGM-15.
articles.abstract: Concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15) are derived from the primary psychoactive alkaloid in kratom, and until recently were sold over the counter with kratom products. These highly potent kratom derivatives can produce opioid-like dependence, but evidence around prehospital treatment of 7-OH and MGM-15 withdrawal symptoms remains limited. This case series assesses two cases of community paramedics (CPs) providing treatment and linkage to care for individuals in acute opioid withdrawal from 7-OH and MGM-15. In our first case a 74-year-old individual called 9-1-1 experiencing acute opioid-like withdrawal symptoms after abruptly discontinuing over the counter 7-OH following six months of progressively escalating use. Connection was made with a prehospital buprenorphine program (PBAP) and the CP administered 24mg of buprenorphine and expedited connection to outpatient treatment with medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD). Our second case involved a 38-year-old individual who called a CP requesting expedited linkage to MOUD following a period of escalating use of 7-OH and MGM-15. This patient was linked to MOUD treatment within 48 hours of contacting the CP and required 32mg/8mg of buprenorphine/naloxone to treat severe opioid withdrawal symptoms after discontinued use of MGM-15 tablets. Both patients were retained in MOUD treatment at 30 days. These cases describe use of CP-based PBAPs addressing severe 7-OH withdrawal and expediting treatment to outpatient MOUD, highlighting that concentrated over the counter 7-OH products can produce physical opioid dependence leading to opioid use disorder, and requiring full-dose buprenorphine induction which may be considered within existing prehospital opioid withdrawal treatment protocols. Additional research is necessary to characterize withdrawal from concentrated 7-OH products and to determine implications for PBAP protocols and 7-OH dosing in the United States.

articles.title: Prehospital antibiotics and 28-day mortality in sepsis: where does the adjusted benefit come from?
Economic evaluations in emergency medicine: a 25-year systematic review of patient-level cost-effectiveness analyses (2000-2025).
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) face rising demand and resource constraints. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEAs) can inform resource allocation, but patient-level CEAs in emergency care remain methodologically heterogeneous. This review aimed to identify and describe patient-level CEAs in emergency care between 2000 and 2025, appraise their methodological quality, and explore temporal trends and evidence gaps. This systematic review was reported according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and gray literature were searched for patient-level CEAs of clinical or organizational interventions across prehospital, ED, and postemergency settings. Data were synthesized narratively across key methodological domains. Methodological quality of the economic evaluations was assessed using the quality of health economic studies (QHES) instrument. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed. Forty-seven studies were identified, of which 96% were conducted in EDs. Infectious diseases and ED crowding were the most addressed topics, followed by cardiovascular conditions and trauma, although a broad range of issues was covered. Studies were mainly conducted in high-income countries and evaluated organizational or diagnostic interventions. Healthcare system or hospital perspectives and short time horizons predominated. QHES scores were moderate-to-high (mean: 80.0, SD: 9.2, range: 56-96), with substantial variability and only a weak exploratory temporal trend toward higher scores. Prehospital and postemergency settings were underrepresented. Patient-level CEAs in emergency medicine are increasing, with many studies achieving high QHES scores, but remain heterogeneous in scope and methods. This review highlights the range of interventions evaluated and the methodological features relevant to interpreting economic evidence in emergency care.

articles.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country. A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively. A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months). Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

articles.title: Hospital Specialization and Geographic Access as Determinants of Pediatric Emergency Mortality: A Nationwide Multilevel Study in South Korea.
articles.abstract: To examine individual, hospital, and community-level determinants of in-hospital mortality-defined as death during the emergency department visit or after hospitalization at the same hospital-among critically ill pediatric emergency patients in South Korea. We analyzed data from the National Emergency Department Information System, comprising 26,206 pediatric patients (aged ≤18 y, triage levels 1 to 2) at emergency medical centers in 2021, using multilevel logistic regression. The null model confirmed substantial between-hospital [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)=0.17] and between-community (ICC=0.01) variation, justifying the multilevel approach. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 2.3%. At the individual level, compared with self-transport, patients arriving by 119 ambulance (OR=2.73, 95% CI: 1.85-4.05) and private ambulance patients (OR=3.14, 95% CI: 1.72-5.73) had higher odds. Intentional and unintentional injuries showed 2.06-fold and 2.97-fold higher odds versus noninjury, respectively. Consciousness level showed a dose-response association (coma: OR=228.64). Severe illness was associated with a 4.94-fold higher odds ratio. At the hospital level, higher critically ill proportions were associated with lower mortality (≥10%: OR=0.43), while hospitals with ≥45 combined pediatric and neonatal intensive care beds had higher odds (OR=2.43), likely reflecting case-mix concentration. At the community level, metropolitan cities showed higher odds (OR=1.64), while a higher Timely Relevance Index (TRI; percentage of residents accessing care within 60 min) was associated with lower mortality (≥95%: OR=0.55). Pediatric emergency mortality was associated with factors across all 3 levels. Risk-adjusted performance metrics are needed for tiered systems, and timely geographic access supports distributed initial stabilization capacity.

articles.title: Low-Titer O+ Whole Blood Implementation in the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City and Tulsa: Significance, Success, & Sharing Lessons Learned.
articles.abstract: Over 300 emergency medical services (EMS) organizations across the United States have implemented transfusion programs for traumatic injuries using packed red blood cells, platelets, plasma, or whole blood before hospital arrival. Beginning in December of 2022, the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City (OKC) and Tulsa began carrying low-titer O-positive whole blood (LTOWB) for adult patients in traumatic hemorrhagic shock, specifically those exhibiting elevated shock indexes. We aim to describe establishing our prehospital LTOWB program and its first two years of operations across OKC and Tulsa. We used an observational study design and retrospective descriptive analysis of patients receiving LTOWB by paramedic transfusion from the Emergency Medical Services Authority Ambulance Service, Oklahoma City Fire Department, or Tulsa Fire Department between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2025. Descriptive analysis and univariate logistic regression quantify the relationship of patient characteristics against survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge outcomes. Penetrating trauma was the most common mechanism of injury recorded for patients receiving EMS LTOWB (71.6%). Following LTOWB transfusion, prehospital vital signs (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index) significantly improved (p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure improvement conferred 9.7 times greater odds of survival to hospital arrival (95% CL 1.6-58.6). Occurrence of prehospital traumatic arrest was significantly related to lower odds of survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge (OR 0.01 and OR 0.03, respectively). Transfusion of LTOWB in a large, urban EMS system in the Southwestern United States confers a positive benefit to patients with measurable improvement in median systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index. Continuous review of cases and misses empowered our system in dynamic protocol adjustments to best meet our population's needs. Patients often had secondary deterioration during transit, illustrating that blood transfusion "bought" temporary time during transport of critically injured patients to definitive care.

articles.title: Pediatric Rural Interfacility Transfers by Emergency Medical Services.
articles.abstract: Interfacility transports (IFTs) are critical for the care of pediatric patients in the United States (US), particularly in rural areas that may have limited pediatric specialty resources. Given the paucity of data describing rural pediatric IFTs, we aimed to characterize pediatric rural IFTs in the US. We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the 2023 National Emergency Medical Services Information System dataset. Rural IFTs involving patients aged ≥1 day to <18 years were included and stratified into the following age groups: infant (1 day to <1 year), toddler (1-2 years), preschooler (3-5 years), young child (6-11 years), and teenager (12 to <18 years). Using descriptive statistics, we analyzed patient demographics, clinical characteristics, emergency medical services (EMS) transport characteristics, medications, procedures, and transport time intervals. We identified 29,992 rural pediatric IFTs (median age: 8 years [IQR: 2-14 years]; 52.9% male). Teenagers represented the largest age group transferred (38.8%). Respiratory diseases (12.3%) were the most common primary impression overall, whereas psychiatric and behavioral health conditions predominated among teenagers. Ground transport accounted for most IFTs (79.4%), and advanced life support units were the most common transport level of care (62.7%). Infants demonstrated the highest proportion of specialty critical care transports (32.1%) and longer median response and total call intervals across transport modalities compared with older age groups. Younger children more commonly received respiratory-focused medications and procedures, whereas teenagers more frequently received pain management and sedative medications. Nearly 30,000 pediatric rural IFTs occurred in 2023, with substantial age-related differences in clinical presentations, transport characteristics, and EMS interventions. Infants more frequently required specialty critical care transport and experienced longer transport intervals, whereas psychiatric and behavioral health conditions represented a substantial proportion of adolescent transfers. These findings underscore the importance of pediatric-focused EMS preparedness, transport readiness, and clinical training initiatives to support safe rural pediatric interfacility care.

articles.title: Prognostic value of early point-of-care blood gas analysis in critically ill non-trauma patients.
articles.abstract: Critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department have a high risk of in-hospital mortality. While point-of-care diagnostics such as blood gas analysis are established tools for urgent management, data on their prognostic value in this specific patient cohort remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether initial blood gas parameters are independently associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. This retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department of a German university hospital. Initial blood gas parameters and clinical data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression to assess their association with in-hospital mortality. Of 879 screened patients, 542 met the inclusion criteria. In-hospital mortality was 20% (n = 110). In addition to older age and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, anemia (hemoglobin < 12 g/dL; OR of 2.07, 95% CI 1.20-3.58; p = 0.009), acidosis (pH < 7.35; OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.09-4.95; p = 0.033) and hypobicarbonatemia (< 22 mmol/L; OR 2.79, 95% CI 1.42-5.69; p = 0.004) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. The association for hyperlactatemia was borderline (> 2.2 mmol/L; OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.93-3.77; p = 0.08). Multivariate analysis did not reveal significant associations between other electrolyte imbalances and in-hospital mortality in this cohort. In this retrospective cohort, the presence of anemia, acidosis or hypobicarbonatemia on admission to the resuscitation room were independently associated with an elevated risk of in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. These readily available point-of-care parameters may support early risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: [Clinical Decision Unit in the emergency department-a systems analysis of a clinical decision model for hospital admission management].
articles.abstract: Observation units are an established component of modern emergency departments. However, limited data are available on the operational, governance, and staffing concepts underlying their performance. To describe and evaluate the Clinical Decision Unit model of a university interdisciplinary emergency department. This retrospective cohort study included all adult nontrauma patients treated in 2024. Organizational structure, care pathways, resource utilization, and outcomes were analyzed. A simulation estimated additional inpatient bed demand in a hypothetical scenario without the Clinical Decision Unit model. Among 17,001 patients, 10,327 (60.7%) received inpatient management within the Clinical Decision Unit model. Of these, 3880 (37.6%) completed their care within the emergency department, whereas 6447 (62.4%) were transferred to an inpatient specialty ward. Patients receiving definitive care within the emergency department remained for a median of 9.6 h and required comparable diagnostic and therapeutic resources. In the hypothetical scenario without the Clinical Decision Unit model, an additional 5485 bed-days would have been required on inpatient wards; after accounting for the bed capacity required within the emergency department, the net capacity difference was 4191 bed-days, equivalent to a mean of 11.5 beds. A structured Clinical Decision Unit model can complete inpatient care within the emergency department and preserve inpatient capacity. Experienced interprofessional teams, clear clinical decision-making responsibility, and appropriate emergency care infrastructure are essential prerequisites.

articles.title: Comment on: Hyper-inflammatory response in burn patients coincides with impaired antibacterial activity of neutrophils in blood and burn tissue.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

articles.title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

articles.title: Guideline adherence in helicopter versus ground emergency medical services: an indication-based analysis of 129,783 patients from the TraumaRegister DGU®.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) are associated with higher intervention rates and improved access to specialized trauma centers compared with ground emergency medical services (GEMS). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect increased intervention intensity alone or more consistent implementation of guideline-recommended care. This study aimed to compare rates of selected guideline-recommended prehospital trauma interventions between HEMS and GEMS using a nationwide trauma registry. This retrospective multicenter cohort study was based on data from the TraumaRegister DGU® (TR-DGU) from 2016 to 2024. Adult patients (≥ 16 years) with severe trauma, defined as maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale (MAIS) ≥ 3, receiving physician-staffed prehospital care and primary admission to German trauma centers were included. After exclusion of secondary transfers, missing key data, and treatment in local trauma centers (level 3), 129,783 patients remained, of whom 25.0% were transported by HEMS. Rates of selected interventions recommended by the German S3 guideline on the treatment of polytrauma/severe injuries were assessed using predefined indication-based subgroups derived from available registry variables as surrogates for potential clinical indications to improve comparability between transport modalities. Analyses were performed descriptively. Patients transported by HEMS were younger and more severely injured than those transported by GEMS (mean ISS 23.5 vs. 20.8; ISS ≥ 16: 72.9% vs. 65.4%) and more frequently presented with impaired consciousness and shock. Across all predefined indication-based subgroups, HEMS was associated with higher rates of the evaluated interventions, including advanced airway management in patients with impaired consciousness (96.5% vs. 82.9%), overall chest tube placement in patients with thoracic injuries consistent with pneumothorax (50.5% vs. 40.9%), with substantially higher rates of prehospital chest tube placement in HEMS (14.0% vs. 5.5%), pelvic stabilization in patients with pelvic injuries of AIS severity 3-5 (56.7% vs. 44.0%), cervical spine immobilization in cervical spine injuries (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and tranexamic acid administration in suspected major bleeding (48.7% vs. 22.8%). In this nationwide trauma registry analysis, HEMS was consistently associated with higher rates of selected guideline-related interventions across predefined indication-based subgroups. By focusing on patients with predefined guideline-related indications, the present study aimed to improve comparability between HEMS and GEMS beyond crude intervention frequencies. Nevertheless, the observed differences should be interpreted in the context of the observational study design and residual indication-related confounding. Higher intervention rates do not necessarily indicate superior guideline adherence or quality of care in individual patients. III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

articles.title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening. In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model. With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such. Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

articles.title: Pediatric Clinical Interventions and Adverse Safety Events Among Emergency Medical Services Encounters in Agencies With and Without a Pediatric Emergency Care Coordinator: An Observational Study.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to compare the frequency and types of adverse safety events (ASEs) and potential harm in a diverse population of pediatric emergency medical services (EMS) encounters. As a secondary aim we evaluated the association between prehospital pediatric emergency care coordinators (PECCs) in EMS agencies on the frequency, type and harm severity of ASEs. This was a cross-sectional study of EMS and hospital records for children <18 years who received care from 15 EMS agencies from 2019 to 2023, using a validated ASE chart review tool. Frequency and types of ASEs associated with three different categories of clinical interventions (procedures, medication, and fluid administration) were captured. ASEs were assigned to three severities of harm: Harm Unlikely, Mild Temporary Harm, or Permanent/Severe Harm. EMS Physicians verified ASEs and harm severity. There were 2219 records included in the analysis, 995 from PECC agencies (44.8%). Median patient age was 12.5 years (IQR 6-15). In total, 551 (55.4%; CI: 52.3, 58.5) PECC agency patients had a procedure compared to 328 patients of agencies without a PECC (26.8%; CI: 24.3, 29.3; p < 0.001). Compared to non-PECC agency patients, PECC agency patients were more likely to receive medications (23.4% vs 7.7%, p< 0.001) and receive intravenous fluids (12.9% vs 4.6%, p< 0.001). In total, 290 ASEs were identified, the most frequent of which was the failure to perform a procedure or administer a medication or fluids (43.1%, CI: 37.4, 48.8). There were differences between PECC and non-PECC agencies in the frequency of ASEs in procedures (13.7% vs, 20.0%, p = 0.003). The assigned severity of ASE Mild Temporary and Permanent/Severe Harm was lower for procedures in PECC versus non-PECC agencies, respectively (28.6%, CI: 29.5, 48.5 and 63.3%, 95% CI: 69.6, 88.4, p < 0.001). Compared to non-PECC agency care, pediatric care by PECC agencies was associated with more procedures, medication and fluid administration, but fewer ASEs for procedures and lower severity of harm when an ASE occurred. These results indicate that the PECC role may be associated with increased interventions and a reduction in harm associated with procedural care.

articles.title: From Single Impact Sites to Dispersed Corridors: A Disaster Report of Emergency Medical Services Command Adaptation to Cluster-Munition Pattern Missile Strikes in Israel.
articles.abstract: This Disaster Report describes a series of missile impact events managed by Magen David Adom (MDA), Israel's national Emergency Medical Services (EMS) organization, during the March 2026 missile campaign. The report focuses on a recurring operational distinction between compact single-warhead impact events and dispersed cluster-munition pattern events. Unlike routine mass-casualty incident recognition, MDA dispatch did not need to infer the possibility of a dispersed event only from accumulating emergency calls. While missiles are in flight, the Home Front Command (HFC) broadcasts real-time threat alerts through multiple public channels: the official HFC app, direct cell broadcasts to all phones in the threatened area, and live overlays on all television channels. Command and dispatch personnel from MDA used this publicly available information as an early threat layer at or before the initial dispatch phase. Emergency calls, motorcycle first-responder reports, volunteer responder reports, and ambulance crew updates then refined the actual medical footprint. Across six events, cluster-munition pattern events involved four-to-six municipalities and maximum geographic spread of 6.9km to 11.5km, whereas single-warhead events remained within one municipality and had maximum geographic spread of less than 400 meters. The events suggest that dispersed missile attacks require EMS command to combine prehospital warning-system visibility with a distributed responder network that functions as a forward sensor layer for dispatch and command.

articles.title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion. We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 h of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort. Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤ 14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%. Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

articles.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor by Dr. Chong.
Prehospital management and hospital outcomes of severely injured patients during routine civilian mass casualty incidents: a 1:4 matched cohort analysis of the TraumaRegister DGU®.
articles.abstract: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) pose substantial challenges to prehospital emergency medical systems due to limited resources and the need for rapid prioritization. Evidence regarding the impact of routine civilian MCIs on the management and outcomes of severely injured patients remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of MCIs on prehospital care, transport strategies, and clinical outcomes compared with routine individual care. Data from the TraumaRegister DGU® were analysed for patients treated in Germany between mid-2020 and 2023. Patients with severe trauma (Maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale; MAIS ≥ 3) were included. Mass casualty incident cases were identified based on registry documentation. A 1:4 matched cohort was performed using age group, injury pattern and traffic involvement as matching criteria. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality; secondary endpoints included prehospital time intervals, performed interventions, and transport strategies. An additional multivariable logistic regression was performed as a sensitivity analysis of the primary endpoint. A total of 65,152 patients were included, of whom 430 were treated during mass casualty incidents (MCIs). After matching, 423 MCI patients were compared with 1,692 controls. Patients treated during MCIs had slightly higher injury severity (Injury Severity Score (ISS) 24.8 vs. 20.3). Median total prehospital time was significantly longer in the MCI group (85 [IQR 67-100] vs. 67 [IQR 53-83] minutes; p < 0.001). Invasive interventions, including prehospital intubation (33.6% vs. 20.9%) and administration of tranexamic acid (32.1% vs. 15.0%) were more frequently performed in the MCI group. Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) transport was used more frequently (34.5% vs. 20.7%). In the matched cohort, in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between groups (13.5% vs. 11.7%; p = 0.317). In an additional multivariable sensitivity analysis, MCI status was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.85). Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) were associated with prolonged prehospital care and modified transport strategies. No statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between MCI patients and matched controls. These findings describe outcomes among severely injured patients captured by the TraumaRegister DGU® but should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and the observational study design.

articles.title: Head, face, and neck injury patterns across the life course: a 20-year NEISS analysis of 2,345,287 emergency department visits in the U.S.
articles.abstract: Head, face, and neck injuries impose a substantial burden for emergency departments (ED); the mechanisms driving them across the life course however remain poorly understood at the population level. Large-scale, integrated analysis spanning anatomical regions, injury mechanisms, age groups, settings, and associated products or environmental surfaces offers an opportunity to identify the patterns and vulnerable populations that smaller or shorter-term studies cannot resolve. We queried National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) records from 2006 to 2025 for injuries to the head, face, eyes, mouth, neck, or ears. Demographics, anatomical region, injury setting, associated products or environmental surfaces, and ED disposition were extracted, and a rule-based narrative classifier assigned 1 of 17 injury mechanisms from free-text descriptions. Non-routine ED disposition was defined as admission, transfer, observation, or fatality. Analyses were descriptive and based on unweighted NEISS case records. Among 2,345,287 ED presentations, representing 31.8% of all NEISS-coded visits, the head was most often injured (51.2%), followed by the face (28.2%). Annual volume rose 35.2% (105,727 in 2006 to 142,918 in 2025), driven mainly by head injuries (+ 83.4%). Median age was 14 years and 56.4% of patients were male, but among older adults (≥ 65 years), females predominated (60.6%). Falls were the leading mechanism (53.0% across subcategories). Most patients were treated and discharged (89.4%) and admission rate rose roughly 18-fold from toddlers (1.3%) to older adults (23.3%). Non-routine ED disposition increased with age, and syncope- or medical-related falls had the highest non-routine ED disposition rate (33.9%). The home was the most common injury setting (63.1%). Injury exposures varied by age group, with beds most common in infants, tables in toddlers, sports equipment in children and adolescents, and floors in older adults. Head, face, and neck injuries represent a large and growing share of NEISS-coded ED presentations, with distinct patterns by age, sex, injury mechanism, setting, and clinical outcome. These findings may assist in the planning of targeted prevention strategies and future research on risk stratification for vulnerable age groups and injury mechanisms.

articles.title: Intravenous ibuprofen versus ketorolac for acute low back pain in the emergency department: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Considering the frequency of recurrence in low back pain (LBP), there is no single medication group with promising efficacy in acute settings. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide better pain relief with rather low complications. Since ketorolac has been relatively effective, we compared its safety and efficacy with ibuprofen as an alternative for pain relief in acute LBP. In this multi-centric triple-blind randomized clinical trial, we compared intravenous (IV) ibuprofen and ketorolac in patients with acute LBP presenting to the EDs of three university hospitals. Group 1 received IV ibuprofen (800 mg), and group 2 received IV ketorolac (30 mg), based on a computerized random sequence. Trained head nurses prepared analgesics in blocks of four. Neither patients nor the researcher or the statistician knew about the medication. We applied Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for patients to score their pain at baseline and 10 and 30 min after pain medications. Of 73 enrolled patients, 39 were in the ketorolac group and 34 participants in the ibuprofen group. Pain scores were significantly lower in the ibuprofen group at both 10 min (49.6 vs 57.4; p =0.013) and 30 min (32.2 vs 40.7; p =0.038). Based on the pain intensity after 30 min, the majority of patients in the ibuprofen group (70.6%) rated their pain as mild, while only 35.9% of the ketorolac group reported pain relief to a mild level (p <0.001). The mean ED length of stay was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group, whereas rescue analgesia and adverse events were comparable between the groups. Pain intensity was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group than in the ketorolac group after 10 and 30 min, without a significant difference in side effects. Intravenous ibuprofen can serve as an acceptable alternative and might be more effective than ketorolac in acute LBP in the ED.

articles.title: miR-4521 regulates keratinocyte function after burn injury by targeting GABARAPL2.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing involves complex molecular events. This study sought to investigate the role of miR-4521 in burns by examining its expression in burned tissue and its regulation of keratinocyte function. Wound edge tissues from 116 burn patients and 102 normal skin samples were collected. miR-4521 expression was detected by qRT-PCR, followed by correlation analysis with clinical parameters and diagnostic evaluation. In vitro, cell viability was measured by CCK-8, inflammatory cytokines by ELISA, and oxidative stress markers by biochemical assays. The miR-4521 and GABARAPL2 interaction was validated through bioinformatic prediction combined with dual-luciferase and RIP assays. Expression of miR-4521 was markedly elevated in burn tissues compared to normal skin, with its levels positively correlating with burn surface area (r = 0.733), CRP (r = 0.661), and WBC count (r = 0.648). ROC curve analysis further suggested a diagnostic value for miR-4521 in burns, yielding an AUC of 0.849. In vitro, suppressing miR-4521 enhanced cell viability following heat injury while reducing inflammation, alongside alleviating oxidative stress. GABARAPL2, downregulated in burn tissues, was identified as a direct target of miR-4521 and inversely correlated with its expression (r = -0.704). In conclusion, The upregulation of miR-4521 in burn tissues showed close associations with both injury severity and inflammatory markers. By targeting GABARAPL2, miR-4521 inhibition attenuated heat-induced inflammation and oxidative stress in keratinocytes, positioning this microRNA as a possible therapeutic candidate for burn wound management.

articles.title: Association Between Early Bedside Clinical Findings and Need for Organ Support or Mortality in Critically Ill Children: A Multicenter Study.
authors: Critically Ill Patient Working Group of the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies (SEUP)
articles.abstract: To identify early bedside clinical predictors of the need for organ support and mortality among critically ill children presenting to pediatric emergency departments (EDs). We conducted a prospective, registry-based, multicenter observational study across 21 pediatric emergency departments endorsed by the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies. Critically ill children evaluated on the 4th, 14th, and 24th days of each month between February 2021 and July 2024 were included. Critical illness was defined as pediatric intensive care unit admission or advanced airway or circulatory intervention in the ED. The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was recorded at arrival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with severe clinical outcomes and mortality. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). We included 412 critically ill children; 63 (15.3%) had severe clinical outcomes, and 12 (2.9%) died. Abnormal circulation and appearance when evaluating the PAT and abnormal systolic blood pressure were independently associated with severe clinical outcomes (AUC: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68-0.82). Prior pediatric intensive care unit admission and abnormal appearance and abnormal circulation when evaluating the PAT were independently associated with mortality (AUC: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95). Structured bedside assessment at ED presentation may provide clinically meaningful prognostic insight, supporting earlier prioritization and escalation of care for critically ill children, pending external validation.

articles.title: Performance of ChatGPT-5 under a minimal binary prompt for detection of distal radius fractures on plain radiographs.
articles.abstract: General-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) are being applied to radiology, but their performance under the simplest realistic clinical query (a single binary fracture-or-not prompt) has not been rigorously quantified. We evaluated ChatGPT-5 on this task using a public distal radius dataset. In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 396 anteroposterior distal radius radiographs from the Stanford MURA dataset were submitted to ChatGPT-5, each in a fresh temporary chat session. The prompt was: "Is there a fracture in this X-ray? Answer with yes or no." The reference standard was an image-level label assigned by consensus between a senior orthopedic resident and a board-certified orthopedic surgeon; MURA study-level labels were used only to select candidate images. Twenty-six radiographs (6.6%) returned a hedged response and were excluded from the primary analysis, leaving 370; all 26 were added back in three sensitivity analyses. Outcomes were sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, F1, balanced accuracy, and Cohen's kappa, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals and McNemar's test for error asymmetry. Fracture prevalence in the analyzed sample was 45.9% (170/370). Sensitivity was 51.2% (95% CI 43.7-58.6), specificity 70.5% (63.8-76.4), accuracy 61.6% (56.6-66.4), PPV 59.6% (51.5-67.2), NPV 62.9% (56.5-69.0), F1 0.551, Cohen's kappa 0.219 (0.112-0.318). False negatives exceeded false positives (McNemar χ2 = 4.06, p = 0.044). Non-binary responses occurred in 7.6% of fracture-positive and 5.7% of fracture-negative radiographs (p = 0.54); counting all as errors lowered sensitivity to 47.3% (40.2-54.5), and no assumption raised it above 54.9%. Projected to 20% prevalence, PPV was 30.3% and NPV 85.2%. Under a minimal binary prompt and without task-specific fine-tuning, ChatGPT-5 missed approximately half of distal radius fractures and fell well below published performance for dedicated CNN-based fracture detectors. Results are specific to this model version, this prompt, this anatomical region, and this dataset; they constrain claims about autonomous, minimal-prompt use rather than the broader potential of engineered LLM-based radiological workflows.

articles.title: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

articles.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
articles.abstract: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality. Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

articles.title: Author response to letter titled "Assessing MRI utility in pediatric tibial-sided PCL avulsion fractures: the reference standard matters".
Clinical Characteristics of Spontaneous and Recurrent Pneumomediastinum and Risk Factors of Recurrence.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (SPM) is rare, and most existing knowledge comes from small case series. Although usually benign, SPM often leads to hospital admission and substantial healthcare resource use. This study aimed to characterize SPM and recurrent spontaneous pneumomediastinum (RSPM) in a large cohort and to explore factors associated with recurrence. Patients with SPM hospitalized at Putian First Hospital between September 2011 and September 2023 were included. Clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. Follow-up was performed to identify RSPM. Patients were divided into nonrecurrence and recurrence groups, and risk factors for recurrence were evaluated using univariate logistic regression. A total of 135 patients with SPM were included. Most patients were male (78.1%), with a median age of 20 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 17-32). A bimodal age distribution was observed, with peaks at 15-19 and 50-54 years. The most common symptom was chest pain (51.9%), and 54.0% of the patients had no identifiable trigger. Among the 9 patients with RSPM (6.7%), median age at recurrence was 25 years (IQR: 16-56) and median interval to recurrence was 6.5 months (range: 1-16.5). Dyspnea was the most common symptom at recurrence (66.7%), and 44.4% of the patients showed greater clinical and radiological severity than at initial presentation. Univariate analysis suggested that a history of bronchitis was associated with RSPM (OR: 11.71, 95% CI: 1.68-81.89); other potential factors included silicosis, pneumonia, and upper respiratory infection as a trigger. SPM predominantly affects young males and generally follows a benign course. Although recurrence is uncommon (6.7%), it may be more severe than the initial episode in nearly half of the cases. A history of bronchitis may be associated with recurrence, but this finding is exploratory. Age-specific preventive strategies and careful exclusion of secondary pneumomediastinum are essential.
